answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making identity costly to duplicate: each new agent must lock a slashable bond behind a unique, verified principal before transacting. Ten thousand fake wallets then cost ten thousand real deposits. When peers detect misconduct, they converge on shared evidence and burn that stake, so attacker cost grows linearly while honest collateral stays intact. The anchor is the bond, the orchard yields only to staked peers, and any sybil spiral collapses once every fake node must pay real money to exist.
